message: Running command: cd /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/assimp && git show 4d5e47a87^:code/AssetLib/3DS/3DSHelper.h | grep -n "struct Texture" -A 50 | head -60

message.content:
Now I see the difference. Before the regression, the `D3DS::Material` copy constructor was explicitly written:

```cpp
Material(const Material &other) :
        mName(other.mName),
        mDiffuse(other.mDiffuse),
        mSpecularExponent(other.mSpecularExponent),
        ...
```

After the regression, it's `= default`. The defaulted copy constructor should be equivalent to the explicit one. But there's a subtle difference: the defaulted copy constructor also copies the vtable pointer (since `Material` has a virtual destructor). Wait, no - the vtable pointer is not copied by the copy constructor; it's set by the constructor itself.

Actually, the key difference is that the defaulted copy constructor of `D3DS::Material` copies ALL members, including any that might have been missed in the explicit version. But the explicit version listed all members, so they should be equivalent.
